summary: This is a documentation/decision-filing-only diff (three YAML files, 228 insertions, 0 deletions, no code, no .github/workflows/** paths, no schema/migration/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security path matches) that correctly classifies as tier1 additive work. I spot-checked the evaluation's evidentiary claims directly against the live repos rather than trusting the self-report: the Analytics Engine findings (analytics-engine.ts's 6 primitives, task-execution-engine.ts's 6 trend_analysis_engine-family call sites, the 5 independent dashboard services including orchestra-analytics-service.ts, the zero-hit registry/builder grep, and the metric-alerts Wave 38 Grafana comment) all check out exactly as described. However, one material claim in the UI Composition Engine evidence is false: the document states projexa's veri-chat/VeriComposer.tsx 'imports @fchecklist/veridian-ui-kit directly,' but the actual file has no such import -- its header comment explains the team investigated adopting the shared composer and explicitly rejected it due to a real behavioral conflict (free-text-required dispatch vs. projexa's deterministic dispatch), keeping a local fork instead. Only the surrounding shell/panel/context pieces (AppShellFrame, PanelShell, veri-chat-context) were actually adopted from veridian-ui-kit -- not the composer/chain-selector component that is the actual subject of the phase's central question. This doesn't necessarily flip the 'acceptable as-is' recommendation, but it overstates cross-product reuse of the specific pattern being evaluated and is exactly the kind of unverified claim that should not reach an Owner-facing decision filing unchallenged. Since this diff ships no code and only files a decision for Owner review (not a unilateral action), the blast radius of the inaccuracy is low and containable at the tier1 additive level -- approving for autonomous merge but flagging the inaccuracy so a follow-up correction can be filed.
issues: ai-os/UI_COMPOSITION_ANALYTICS_ENGINE_EVALUATION_2026-07-24.yaml's ui_composition_engine_evaluation section claims projexa's src/components/veri-chat/VeriComposer.tsx 'imports @fchecklist/veridian-ui-kit directly' as evidence of live cross-product reuse of the composer/chain-selector pattern. Verified false: the file's own header comment says the team investigated adopting the shared VeriComposer and explicitly kept a local fork due to a real requirements conflict (shared component requires non-empty free text before dispatch; projexa's dispatch is deterministic with no required user text). The file has zero veridian-ui-kit imports. Only VeriChatPanel.tsx (PanelShell) and veri-chat-context.tsx (createVeriChatContext) genuinely import the shared package among the veri-chat/* files listed -- the specific composer/chain-selector pattern the phase question is actually about was NOT successfully reused as claimed. Recommend a follow-up correction to the filed Owner decision so the evidence presented is accurate, though this does not block tier1 approval of the current additive, no-code diff.
